HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is on Buspar, started by Dr. Brown, for anxiety. Buspar is new medication. Patient reports anxiety was severe in November and December, described as "brutal," occurring primarily during the day at work. At that time, patient was started on Singulair by Dr. Ward, who noted that Singulair can cause anxiety; patient uncertain if this contributed to symptoms. In November and December, anxiety would spike the week before menses, then progressed to random spikes without clear trigger. Currently on Buspar with improvement. Patient attributes anxiety to multiple possible factors including medication effect (Singulair), hormonal factors related to menstrual cycle, work stress related to "golive" in November-December, and work-related stress from COVID response (leading process for delivering COVID results to patients, helping establish evaluation centers and COVID clinic). Patient reported feeling selfish and guilty about experiencing anxiety given that others were on front lines.

Patient discontinued Camila birth control due to significant appetite stimulation and constant hunger; now feeling better. Reports weight loss over past six months.

Patient has breast lumps that appear smaller than before but still present. Reports soreness in left breast. History of breast soreness during breastfeeding with clogged duct and other issues.

Reports vaginal itching and discomfort, managed with topical cream used weekly with good response. Currently needs refill.
